questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction once you have avoided the hazard.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see better and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What headlight should you use in fog?

options.text: Alternate between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in foggy conditions. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Stay silent and not talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay silent and not talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, so your motorcycle will not respond as quickly. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, and increase your distance behind other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Should motorcycle riders wear hearing protection?

options.text: Yes, always wear it to prevent hearing damage.
No, it blocks important sounds like horns and sirens.
No, a helmet provides enough protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, always wear it to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing loss, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still allowing you to hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: What group formation is best for riding in curves, turns, or entering a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally best for group riding, use single-file formation when riding through curves, turns, or entering and exiting highways.

questions.question: If one rider wants to go faster than the group, what should happen?

options.text: Let the faster rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up and let each rider choose their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the faster rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than others in the group, let them go ahead and meet at an agreed-upon location later.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake immediately and reapply it smoothly.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp hard on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever firmly with all four fingers, gradually applying more force.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol level (BAC) is a person age 21 or older legally intoxicated?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person who is 21 or older with a blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane if there is traffic. Swerving to avoid a small animal can cause you to hit another vehicle. A collision with another car is more dangerous than hitting a small animal.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate to leave the dog behind.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This is especially helpful when riding through areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more slippery than other surfaces.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: If the rear tire locks on a surface with good grip, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You should still be able to steer your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for groups to stay close while maintaining safe space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of the following helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce speed, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Follow tire tracks left by cars instead of using the center lane. Watch for oil spots, loose gravel, and other hazards that make roads slippery.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders not wearing helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three major factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: They do not need to reach the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always ride directly behind the operator. A child in front may not balance properly and could get in the way of the controls.

questions.question: How do you stop a motorcycle in a straight line with maximum braking power?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum braking power comes from applying both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.

questions.question: What should you do when turning left on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward to make the motorcycle lean in that direction.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. You need more distance to stop safely in these conditions.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They are a good substitute for a face shield.
They are a good substitute for goggles.
They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Stay flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes smoothly. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to get out of a wobble.
